issues.legal_issue: A decree for specific performance was properly granted where the concurrent findings established a genuine agreement, the purchaser’s readiness and performance, and the seller’s breach.
material_facts: The trial court found the sale agreement genuine and found that the purchaser was ready and willing to perform and had performed his part of it.
The courts found that the seller did not execute the sale deed and thereby breached the agreement.
The trial court and first appellate court granted specific performance, and the High Court affirmed.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent decision granting specific performance was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 makes the grant of specific performance discretionary. The plaint contained the averments required by Section 16(c) of that Act, and the courts found the purchaser ready and willing to perform. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and agreement_found_genuine and purchaser_ready_and_willing and purchaser_performed_part and seller_breached_agreement

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The purchaser brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.agreement_found_genuine: The courts found that the agreement was genuine.
predicates.purchaser_ready_and_willing: The courts found that the purchaser was ready and willing to perform his part of the agreement.
predicates.purchaser_performed_part: The courts found that the purchaser performed his part of the agreement.
predicates.seller_breached_agreement: The courts found that the seller failed to perform his part of the agreement.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit has these findings, the decree granting specific performance is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent findings of fact cannot be disturbed in a Supreme Court appeal merely by reappreciating the evidence when those findings are not perverse or contrary to the evidence, pleadings, or law.
material_facts: The trial court, first appellate court, and High Court all found that the agreement was genuine and that the purchaser was ready and willing to perform.
Those courts rejected the seller’s claim that the agreement was forged after considering the parties’ evidence.
The Supreme Court found no basis to treat the concurrent findings as perverse or contrary to the evidence, pleadings, or law.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to reappreciate the evidence or disturb the concurrent findings and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal under Article 136 of the Constitution, concurrent findings of fact are binding where they are not perverse and are not contrary to the evidence, pleadings, or law. The Court also stated that such findings bind the High Court in a second appeal. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: supreme_court_appeal_after_concurrent_findings and findings_based_on_evidence and not findings_perverse and not findings_contrary_to_evidence_pleadings_or_law

predicates.supreme_court_appeal_after_concurrent_fi: A party brought a Supreme Court appeal after multiple lower courts made concurrent findings of fact.
predicates.findings_based_on_evidence: The lower courts reached their findings after considering the evidence.
predicates.findings_perverse: The findings are so unreasonable that no judicial person could have reached them.
predicates.findings_contrary_to_evidence_pleadings_: The findings conflict with the evidence, the parties’ pleadings, or the law.

issues.definition: When a Supreme Court appeal follows evidence-based concurrent findings that are not perverse or contrary to the evidence, pleadings, or law, those findings are not disturbed.
